decides_short.text: Fact {rank-fact}: read straight from the code.
Inferred {rank-exact}, {rank-assumed} or {rank-suffix}: a fixed rank per match rule, not a probability.
Unknown: listed, never guessed, never counted as zero.
Precise or Best effort: labelled per area, with the reason.

decides_intro: Everything Graphvein shows carries a label that says how it was found. The number next to a link is a fixed rank per match rule, not a probability.

decides.title: Fact
decides.body: Read straight from the code, for example a route registration. A fact always has the number {rank-fact}.

decides.title: Inferred, with a fixed rank
decides.body: Two things matched by a rule, for example a frontend call to a route by its URL. The number is a fixed rank per match rule, not a probability: an exact path match is {rank-exact}, or {rank-assumed} when the call’s base URL is assumed rather than proven, and a path suffix match is {rank-suffix}.

decides.title: Unknown
decides.body: The code does not say, for example a URL built at runtime. Graphvein lists these instead of guessing, and never counts an unknown as zero or as “no change”.

decides.title: Precision labels
decides.body: Each area is labelled Precise or Best effort. Precise never means complete. Precise structure covers four languages (Go, Python, Rust and TypeScript/JavaScript); calls are Best effort in every language.

verified_short.text: Claim contract tables: one row per modelled form.
Benchmark method and every run published.
Golden fixtures and tests, CI on Windows, macOS and Linux.

verified_intro: Every claim the site makes points to public material you can check.

verified.title: Claim contract tables
verified.body: Where an extractor covers a large language or framework surface, every form it models has exactly one row, and every other form falls to a single unknown default branch. Tests keep the code and the tables {claims-one-to-one}.

verified.title: Decision records
verified.body: Design decisions are recorded as ADRs: context, options considered, decision, consequences and known gaps.

verified.title: Golden fixtures and tests
verified.body: Extractors and linkers are tested against committed fixtures with golden output.

verified.title: CI on Windows, macOS and Linux
verified.body: CI runs the main module on all three, with cgo disabled.

verified.title: Benchmark method and raw results
verified.body: Questions, method, every run’s row and final answer are published. Answers are graded by a script against facts verified from the source code; no language model judges an answer.

verified.title: Release checksums and provenance
verified.body: Each release lists a checksum for every archive, and every archive has a build provenance attestation from the release workflow.

footer: No cookies, no tracking, no third-party scripts or fonts.
